comparison_evidence.quote: Crossbow: Oryn's (carried two years), handed to Brom at the stone in Ch10's afternoon (off-page seam).

findings.consequence: The repair delivers the required four underside hits by fielding three crossbows — Seln's own, Oryn's, and a separate 'Brom's' — where the frozen state records exactly one in the unit's hands. 'Brom's bow' and 'Oryn's crossbow' are the same weapon in Chapter 18 ('Brom's bow') and Chapter 19 ('Brom, with the bow across his chest'), and Seln carries a knife on the Stair, not a bow. Read against that inventory, Lira has one bow rather than two, the second hit vanishes, and the four bolts the climax counts become three — which collapses the very obligation this repair was staged to satisfy. A reader tracking the crew's kit hits the contradiction inside the decisive exchange.
findings.repair_target: Reconcile the chapter's crossbow inventory with the frozen state: either establish on the page where the second and third bows came from, or stage Lira's two hits from the single recorded weapon (a reload she can perform one-armed, or a spanner working beside her) and give Seln a weapon the previous chapters have put in his hands.

draft_evidence.quote: Nobody asked why. Ten paces past the stake, at the hall's own lip where the wall's foot met the water, a second bar of iron stood out of the mud, and it was not straight. It was bent — the top of it a hand's height off true, and bent the way a nail bends when a thing under it pushes up, not the way a nail bends when a thing above it pushes down. Seln had seen it from the line. Seln had not gone to it.

comparison_evidence.quote: The trials could not be run from the line; it was a hundred and seventy meters out in the marsh and nothing a man could throw would reach the water from it.

findings.consequence: The bent bar is fixed at two incompatible places. It is ten paces from a perimeter stake that line 15 puts 'in the reeds ten paces along the line', and it is simultaneously at the hall's lip, which line 29's repaired number puts a hundred and seventy meters further in and which line 13 frames as two hundred meters of marsh. The same paragraph then reports its inclination to a hand's height and the direction of the bend from a viewpoint that has not crossed the line. The repair sharpened the collision by putting an explicit distance on the page, and the bar is load-bearing evidence for the water-bound rule the fight depends on, so a reader who tries to place it loses confidence in the teaching sequence.
findings.repair_target: Place the bent bar once, consistently with the hundred-and-seventy-meter figure and the two-hundred-meter perimeter — either move the close observation to the causeway crossing later that afternoon, or drop the 'ten paces past the stake' locator and let Seln read it at distance in the terms distance allows.

strengths: Yes: the worldbuilding is done through mechanism and use, and the repair strengthened it. The Quieting is a marked stride and a healer checking her hands; Compact history is a scaled stake and a bar bent from below; road lore reaches the page through a patient whose leg was in the animal's mouth; and the creature is learned by two stones, a count, and a held point rather than described. Nothing is explained that could be demonstrated.

Yes: the fight is memorably choreographed and terrain is load-bearing far past the two-beat minimum — and the twelve-stride repair made it drawable rather than merely vivid. The causeway forces the approach; standing weight triggers the first strike; the wet boot-wide coping causes Brom's slip; the shallows permit the skipping movement; the broken centre's depth is both where the animal turns and where the point is laid. The win is writable as: Cael removed the wyrm's ability to choose its target by giving the flooded floor one point that never moved.

The teaching sequence remains the chapter's best fairness work, and the relocation to the outer coping cost it nothing. Two stone behaviours isolate settled weight from sound and from motion; the Anchor trial then proves the exact interaction the climax needs, timed by a researcher who does not trust a count she did not make; and Karis's and Cael's fixed lines still distinguish two mental models of the same finding.

Oryn is still a healer in action rather than a fighter converted for a set piece. She enters the water because a patient is falling, takes the shortest line, applies the movement rule the afternoon taught, and pays the reserve cost outside the line. 'So are you' lands because the practical route has been her relationship vocabulary since Chapter 18.

The found-family division of competence survives the repair intact and should be protected in any further pass: Brom supplies weight and wall knowledge, Seln converts observation into a rule and then reloads under time, Karis copies because the evidence is the objective, Lira adapts one-armed, Oryn reaches the patient, Cael turns the rule. No two of them solve the floor the same way.

The packet's restraint holds everywhere it is tested: the wyrm is neither killed nor read, the tenth fragment is explicitly spent on no one, no mind or Path is assigned to the animal, no Quieting theory is approached, and the chapter trusts dialogue after Chapter 20's log.

The repairs are surgical and preserve voice. The water-bound rule now rests on a single piece of evidence read correctly ('There's no mark of anything on the top of the ridges but the weather'); the release of the fixed point is timed to the last bolt rather than to a bolt count; the Iron read's cost is entered in the same ledger register the book has used since Book 1; and the elapsed-time correction to five days reconciles cleanly with Chapter 19's mend and Chapter 20's dated day.

Production hygiene remains clean: metadata and summary-family greps return zero, every named section 9 tic returns zero, banned registers and feeling- and growth-declarations return zero, no single-word paragraphs, no new named entity, attribution survives audio, and the final beat type differs from Chapter 20's.
